title: Grain, Drag, Ink, Glow & Morph
description: A Bayer-dither field, a drag-to-arrange bento dashboard, halftone ink type, cursor-lit embossed buttons, and a morphing preview card.

drops.title: Ordered Dither Field
drops.description: Three animated plasma fields quantized live through a recursively-built Bayer threshold matrix in real time.
drops.concept: Ordered dithering is the 1970s print-reprographics trick of thresholding a continuous-tone image against a fixed matrix instead of adding random noise — it's having a moment again as a retro/pixel-art shader effect in 2026 component libraries. This drop builds the Bayer matrix recursively at runtime (2×2 → 4×4 → 8×8 via the standard quadrant-tiling formula) and re-quantizes an animated multi-level plasma field against it every frame, with the cursor locally boosting brightness to push the dither pattern around.

interaction.mouse: Move over any field to locally brighten and push the dither pattern
interaction.click: Switch Bayer order, drag sliders for cell size / speed, toggle cursor push
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across a field for the same brighten effect

drops.title: Drag-Bento Dashboard
drops.description: A CSS Grid dashboard where tiles drag-to-rearrange with real collision resolution and auto-compaction.
drops.concept: Draggable, resizable, auto-compacting widget grids — popularized by gridstack.js and now standard in Notion, Linear and Vercel-style customizable dashboards — are the layout backbone of the 2026 'organic bento' trend. This reimplementation tracks widgets as (x,y,w,h) grid-unit rectangles, shows a live snap-preview ghost while dragging, resolves overlaps by pushing colliding tiles downward, then runs a compaction pass that pulls every tile as far up as it can go — all in vanilla pointer events over CSS Grid, no library.

interaction.mouse: Drag a tile to move it, drag its corner grip to resize
interaction.click: Use the panel to change column count, gap, shuffle or reset
interaction.touch: Press and drag a tile or its corner grip — same pointer-event path as mouse

drops.title: Halftone Type
drops.description: Headlines rasterized to canvas, sampled on a dot grid, and redrawn as brightness-sized ink circles.
drops.concept: Halftone dot printing is the newspaper/riso trick 2026's brutalist-print aesthetic keeps borrowing back. Each headline is drawn once to a hidden canvas at full weight; the alpha channel is sampled on a regular grid to build a dot list, then redrawn as filled circles whose radius scales with sampled brightness — one static, one with cursor-proximity dot inflation for a 'flashlight reveals more ink' feel, and one that breathes on a sine timer like slowly re-wetting ink.
drops.source: Banyapon Poolsawas — "Creating Halftone Dot Art with JavaScript" (Medium)

interaction.mouse: Hover the duotone headline to swell nearby dots
interaction.click: Drag the panel sliders for dot spacing, cursor boost, breathe speed
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across the duotone headline for the same swell

drops.title: Cursor-Lit Relief
drops.description: Bump-mapped panels lit by a real SVG fePointLight that tracks the cursor across each material.
drops.concept: feSpecularLighting and fePointLight are original SVG filter primitives that compute an actual Phong lighting model against an alpha-channel bump map — a technique older than most of the web, now back in fashion for the 'jelly, chrome, clay' tactile-material trend of 2026 UI. Three panels use the same light-source rig with different bump sources and lighting parameters: brushed steel blends feTurbulence noise into its bump map for a hammered texture with a tight specular exponent, warm clay uses a soft low-exponent highlight on a smooth bump, and obsidian glass uses a razor-sharp exponent on a nearly flat surface. Moving the cursor updates the shared fePointLight's x/y per-panel every frame.
drops.source: CSS-Tricks — "A Look at SVG Light Source Filters"

interaction.mouse: Move across any panel — the specular highlight tracks the cursor as a light source
interaction.click: Toggle auto-orbit to sweep the light automatically; drag the light-height slider
interaction.touch: Drag a finger across a panel to sweep the highlight

drops.title: Morphing Preview Card
drops.description: One shared floating card glides, resizes and cross-fades between six hover triggers instead of reopening.
drops.concept: Base UI's Preview Card primitive (from the MUI team) popularized hover-cards that open on a real delay and reposition per-trigger via anchor logic — but the detail that makes it feel expensive is what happens when the pointer moves directly from one trigger to a neighboring one while the card is already open: instead of closing and replaying the open animation, the same DOM node retargets instantly, sliding to the new anchor point and cross-fading its content. This build reimplements that state machine — open-delay timer, close-delay timer, and an 'already engaged' fast-path — from scratch with plain timers and CSS transitions.

interaction.mouse: Hover a chip to open its card after a short delay; glide to another chip to morph instantly
interaction.click: Tune open/close delay and preferred side in the debug panel
interaction.touch: Long-press (~380ms) a chip to open; tap elsewhere to dismiss
